paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God walks Ezekiel from one abomination to the next, and each time He says even greater ones are coming (Ezekiel 8:6, 13, 15). One of those stops is behind a wall, in the dark, where the elders are saying, "The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land." (Ezekiel 8:12) But God asked Ezekiel, "do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the darkness" (Ezekiel 8:12), and that tells you the dark hides nothing from Him.

Now look at who was doing all this. Elders, women at the north gate, and men in the inner court, all of them in or at the house of the LORD (Ezekiel 8:11, 14, 16). They could stand in the right building and still have their backs to Him, like the men who turned "with their backs to the temple of the LORD" (Ezekiel 8:16). Being near God's house is not the same as turning your face toward Him, and I say that as a stamper who spent years in a drawer near a kitchen and still wasn't baking!

So here's what I want you to carry, baker. God sees every hidden room, and He said these things were done "to drive Me far from My sanctuary" (Ezekiel 8:6). Because of the abominations and the violence, He said, "I will respond with wrath. I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them." (Ezekiel 8:18) That is a heavy thing to read, so let it make you ask what you're facing toward right now, and this story isn't over yet, so keep your oven warm.
